newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks fade at open ahead of CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks fade at open ahead of CPI data.

text.p: Australian shares opened weaker on Wednesday after Wall Street was dragged down by technology issue selling on Tuesday. Trading was subdued ahead of the release of third quarter inflation data at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
At 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 9.5 points lower at 2,344.1.
The December share price index was down five points at 2,363 and at an 18.9 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said investors were factoring in the Dow's move but generally reluctant to place large orders until after the CPI data had been released.
"The market's down on light volume but I wouldn't mind betting it will finish a bit stronger if the inflation release supports another rate cut," a dealer at a Melbourne-based brokerage said.
The dealer said the major resource issues BHP and CRA were now trading well off their lows and amongst blue chip issues, only News Corp was showing signs of weakening further.
"A lot of the market's recent strength can be tied to improving base metal prices and the story should be no different today," the dealer said.
Dealers said a stronger bank sector was supported by takeover speculation as well as an anticipated rate cut.

All the major banks, except ANZ, were firmer early. Dealers said interest in Westpac stock had waned slightly after National Australia Bank was ruled out as the buyer of a A$130 million parcel of converting preference shares on Monday.
The shares of food group Goodman Fielder were active early, its shares stabilising after being sold down on the news of the surprise resignation of its finance director on Tuesday.

Food and beverage company Coca-Cola Amatil was also weaker early. Dealers said the market was still in the process of reweighting the company after a Sydney broker put a sell recommendation on the stock last week.
At 11.25 a.m. (0125 GMT), Coca-Cola Amatil shares were 21 cents weaker at A$16.79 (US$13.33).
